correctness.rationale: The replacement theorem is the anticommuting census and parity comparison, using the known commuting census. Arrow products have independent length-two path coefficients, and J³=0 makes both length-two coordinate vectors free. On each support, there are q−1 vector choices per projective color, and the equations are equality for commuting and reflection [a:b]↦[a:−b] across each anticommuting transition. This works for either path orientation and for loops. A spanning tree propagates the colors; odd cycle or loop consistency forces exactly the two coordinate colors in odd characteristic. Empty support and isolates have the indicated contributions. Comparing every summand gives strict inequality from the full support when a nonbipartite component exists. Signs on a bipartition transform each path equation by a nonzero scalar; characteristic two is the identity comparison for any graph. The acyclic example has exactly the seven named length-two paths, and only its full support contributes to the deficit, giving q^14(q−1)^8. Independently enumerated both path-equation counts and support-component counts for all two-vertex endpoint multisets of up to three indexed arrows over F2, F3 and F4 (105 cases), factoring out the free length-two coordinates. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed; its seven-arrow odd-field results are algebraic deficit checks, not exhaustive runs.

evidence: The Resultary centralizer-rank finding includes the commuting formula for all quivers here. The induced-subgraph polynomial provides the graph invariant. Gawell–Richey Xantcha impose anticommutativity in the defining ideal.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Imposed algebra relations are not equations for two varying elements of a fixed truncated path algebra. The known centralizer theorem is a covering result for the commuting side, not for plus signs on supported edges.

evidence: The prior commuting census uses the identical equality-of-projective-lines argument. It does not determine whether opposite-sign transport closes consistently around an odd cycle; in particular its loop-blind invariant does not give the odd-q equality criterion.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the commuting reduction exactly. The replacement uses the involution's two fixed colors to resolve the plus equation, including an acyclic quiver whose arrows nevertheless close an odd transition cycle.

evidence: The commuting count is q^(2p)Q(G;q−1,q+1) with graph loops ignored. Anticommutation is a supported graph homomorphism count to a target of two looped colors and (q−1)/2 disjoint two-vertex edges.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The latter counts color transport by an involution, not the ordinary same-color Potts constraint. Balance of the all-negative signed support is bipartiteness. A general color-transport reformulation supplies a counting interpretation, not by itself a prior quiver radical pair count.

evidence: The general commuting census is an exact earlier indexed match despite the loop convention; the parallel-arrow record is a narrower commuting analogue. No inspected matching record gives the anticommuting formula and deficit.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Component counts ignore inserted loops, whereas the nonbipartite counts in the anticommuting formula do not. Hence different graph notation does not save the original commuting contribution. There is no numerical table claim beyond the illustrative deficits.

originality.rationale: For the original bundle the novelty assertion about the general quiver-to-graph commuting census fails: the earlier matched record gives exactly that census and reduction. The replacement removes it as a contribution rather than appending a disclaimer to the original claim. The anticommuting census, equality criterion, and acyclic odd-transition witness survive the prior comparison. They apply a twisted projective constraint to a different radical-pair equation and do not claim the component polynomial or an abstract signed-coloring principle as new.
residual_risks: A signed-involution/two-fixed-color formulation may already overlap the component count; the revised claim is specifically the quiver radical application and comparison. Earlier literature stating that application in other terms has not been ruled out exhaustively.

value.rationale: In a natural finite-dimensional algebra, the plus equation yields a structural discriminator invisible to ordinary component counts and to directed acyclicity. The exact odd-field inequality for every nonbipartite transition graph, the opposite-sign linear equivalence in the bipartite case, and the explicit acyclic witness distinguish two closely related loci rather than merely re-evaluating the known commuting polynomial.
